q: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210 replaced which earlier document?
n: Doc. 210 formally supersedes the older 1979 fee guideline, updating it to the post-R.A. 9266 regulatory framework. [Source: Rule I, Sec. 1]

q: Doc. 210 was promulgated in compliance with which PRBoA issuance?
n: The Guidelines were prescribed under PRBoA Resolution No. 3, s. 2010; a later Resolution No. 6, s. 2016 merely published it in the Official Gazette. [Source: Cover page]

q: Under a DAEDS contract, architectural design services constitute what percentage of the corresponding fee?
n: Since architectural design is the core scope, it makes up 60% of the full DAEDS fee, with engineering/allied services making up the rest — this is also why DADS rates are 60% of DAEDS rates. [Source: Sec. 4, 4.1.1.3]

q: "PPCC" refers to which basis for the % of PCC method?
o: Probable Project Construction Cost, fixed at signing
n: PPCC is a mutually-agreed estimate using unit-price parameters (market rate/sqm) fixed at signing — distinct from the Awarded (bid-based) or Final (cost-records-based) PCC. [Source: Sec. 4, 4.1.1.2]

q: In the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method, the multiplier (M) typically ranges between:
n: The multiplier compensates for overhead, benefits, contingencies, capital interest, and profit; it typically falls between 1.5 and 2.5 depending on office set-up and complexity. [Source: Sec. 4, 4.3.8; Annex A, Multiplier]

q: For Pre-Design Services, what acceptance fee should the Architect request upon signing, based on the agreed Professional Fee?
n: The 5% acceptance fee secures the engagement before pre-design work begins and is credited against the agreed Professional Fee. [Source: Sec. 5.3]

q: For a Group 1 building (e.g., a warehouse) with a PCC of P50.0M or less, the DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee is:
n: Group 1 covers the simplest building types (warehouses, garages, industrial plants), so it carries the lowest base rate among the groups at 5% for PCC up to P50M. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 1]

q: COMPUTATION: A Group 1 building has a PCC of P80,000,000. Using the DAEDS bracket (P2,500,000 + 4% of excess over P50.0M), what is the Professional Fee?
n: Excess over P50M = P30M; 4% × P30M = P1,200,000; add the P2,500,000 base for the bracket to get P3,700,000. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 1 DAEDS table]

q: What is the DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee for Group 4 (single-detached residences, duplexes, row-houses, small apartments/townhouses)?
n: Residential work (Group 4) is compensated at a flat 10% of PCC for DAEDS, higher than Groups 1--3 since it isn't bracketed by cost. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 4]

q: Group 5 covers monumental buildings (museums, memorials, expo/fair buildings). Its DAEDS RPF is:
n: Group 5 (monumental/highly decorative buildings) demands the most consummate design skill of the flat-rate groups, so it carries a 12% DAEDS rate versus 10% for ordinary residences. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 5]

q: SITUATIONAL: Under Group 6 (Repetitive Construction, same plan re-used without amendment), what RPF applies to the third (3rd) building?
n: The scale steps down with each repeat build (100% → 50% → 40% → 30%) since design effort is already spent; the 3rd building falls at 40%. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 6]

q: Under Group 7 (Housing Project, DAEDS), how is the fee for the 2nd--10th unit computed?
o: 10% of PCC per unit, no reduction
Fee for 1 unit + 50% of RPF per additional unit
Fee for 1 unit + 40% of RPF per additional unit
Flat 6% of PCC regardless of unit count
n: The first unit is billed at the full 10% DAEDS rate; each additional unit from the 2nd--10th adds only 50% of that RPF, reflecting reduced design effort per repeat unit. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 7]

q: Group 8 (extensive detail — built-in components, architectural interiors, development planning/design) carries a flat RPF of:
n: Group 8 covers highly detailed interior/built-in work, warranting the highest flat rate among the building-type groups at 15% of PCC. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 8]

q: For Group 9 (alterations, renovations, retrofits to existing Group 1--5 buildings), compensation is:
o: Reduced by 50% of the applicable RPF
Increased by 50%, i.e., 150% of the applicable RPF
Fixed at 12% of PCC regardless of group
Charged at the Group 8 rate of 15%
n: Renovation/retrofit work requires more effort per unit of construction cost than new construction, so the applicable RPF (from Groups 1--5) is surcharged by 50%. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 9]

q: Under Group 10 (opinion/advice on technical matters), the chargeable RPF shall not be less than:
n: This is a floor rate for consultation/opinion work — P1,000/hour minimum, rising with the scope and location of the engagement. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 10]

q: SITUATIONAL: Under the standard payment schedule, what is the CUMULATIVE percentage of the Professional Fee due upon completion of Design Development Services?
n: Cumulative payments build up: 5% at signing, +15% at Schematic Design = 20%, +20% at Design Development = 40% cumulative. [Source: Sec. 6.4]

q: What CUMULATIVE percentage of the PF is due upon completion of the Contract Documents phase?
n: The Contract Documents phase is the largest single billing (50% of PF), bringing the running total from 40% to 90% cumulative — only the 10% Construction-completion payment remains. [Source: Sec. 6.4]

q: SITUATIONAL: If the Construction Phase is suspended for more than six (6) months, what happens to the fee for the remaining Periodic Construction Supervision work?
n: A long suspension (over 6 months) disrupts the Architect's workflow and staffing, so the remaining periodic supervision fee is doubled to compensate for the disruption. [Source: Sec. 6.4.10]

q: The Recommended Professional Fee for Full-Time Construction Supervision Services (SPP Doc. 204-A) is:
n: Full-time supervision is a dedicated on-site role, priced as a modest percentage band (1--1.5%) of PCC, separate from and additional to the design fee. [Source: Sec. 8.3]

q: The Recommended Professional Fee for Construction Management Services (SPP Doc. 204-B) is:
n: Construction Management carries broader managerial responsibility than plain supervision, so its RPF band (1.5--3%) is higher than the 1--1.5% for Full-Time Supervision. [Source: Sec. 9.3]

q: For Post-Construction Services as Building Administrator (SPP Doc. 205), the RPF is expressed as:
n: Post-construction building administration is compensated as value-pricing tied to revenue generated, not to construction cost — hence the fee is a % of gross rental, not of PCC. [Source: Sec. 10.3]

q: As overall Project Manager under Comprehensive Architectural Services (SPP Doc. 206), the Architect's RPF is:
n: As overall Project/Development Manager overseeing a multidisciplinary team, the Architect earns 2--5% of PCC for that PM role, separate from any Regular Design Services fee on the same project. [Source: Sec. 11.3]

q: Under Design-Build Services by Administration (SPP Doc. 207), the RPF is:
n: Design-Build by Administration bundles construction-phase responsibility onto the Architect, billed at 7% of PCC on top of (exclusive of) the Regular Design Services fee. [Source: Sec. 12.4]

q: Under Design-Build on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost, the RPF is:
o: 10% of PCC, or built into the Guaranteed Maximum Cost
n: Taking on cost-overrun risk under a Guaranteed Maximum Cost commands a higher rate than Administration mode — 10% of PCC, or it may instead be built directly into the GMC figure. [Source: Sec. 12.4]

q: For Physical Planning (Site Development Planning, SPP Doc. 203), the RPF for the first five (5) hectares or less is:
n: P50,000/ha equates to P5.00/sqm net to the Architect for the first 5 hectares, before the rate steps down for larger areas. [Source: Sec. 7.3.2, 7.3.2.1]

q: If the Owner hires Specialist Consultants (SCs) separately for a project under Specialized Architectural Services, the Architect's coordination fee is:
n: When the Owner engages SCs directly (bypassing the Architect), the Architect still coordinates their input and is paid 5% of the SC's fee for that coordination role — the same principle recurs under Secs. 8.5 and 9.5. [Source: Sec. 7.2.3 (also Secs. 8.5, 9.5)]

q: Under Sec. 16, interest on fees unpaid more than 30 days from billing is charged based on:
o: The prevailing rate set by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP)
n: Rather than a fixed statutory rate, the interest rate floats with the BSP's prevailing rate, as mutually agreed by Architect and Client, once billing is over 30 days unpaid. [Source: Sec. 16]

q: Disputes over the Service Agreement that reach arbitration are handled through which body, per Sec. 19?
n: Under R.A. 9285 and E.O. 1000, unresolved disputes escalate to CIAC arbitration (after negotiation/mediation fail), with CIAC bound to resolve within six months. [Source: Sec. 19.2]

q: In Annex A, "Cost of Work (CoW)" as a fee basis applies specifically to which type of service?
n: "Cost of Work" is a defined term specific to Specialized Architectural Services (interiors, acoustics, lighting, site works, landscaping), used as the fee base instead of PCC. [Source: Annex A, Cost of Work]

q: What does "RPF" stand for in this document?
n: RPF is the reference/benchmark fee the Guidelines set for each building type and service, factoring in scope and adjustment factors. [Source: Annex A, xviii; Annex B]

q: COMPUTATION (Sec. 4.1.2 worked example): A hi-rise office has 10,000 sqm GFA at P30,000/sqm historical PCC and a 6% PCC fee, plus 2,000 sqm non-GFA area billed at 50% of the GFA rate. What is the GFA portion of the fee?
n: GFA fee = unit PCC × fee rate × area = P30,000 × 0.06 × 10,000 sqm = P18,000,000; the non-GFA portion is computed separately and added on top. [Source: Sec. 4.1.2, Worked Example]

q: SITUATIONAL (Annex D, Sorsogon Medical Center — Building Group 3): After applying the Level 1 Specialist, BIM, new construction technology, third-party certification, DOH approval, multiple-bid, and other adjustment factors to the 7.0% DAEDS base, the adjusted sub-total fee rate becomes:
n: Adjustment factors (Level 1 Specialist 0.50 + BIM 0.10 + new tech 0.10 + certification 0.10 + DOH approval 0.10 + multiple bids 0.25 = 1.05%) are added to the 7.0% base to reach an 8.05% sub-total, which then drives the bracketed peso computation. [Source: Annex D — DAEDS Worksheet]

q: Per Sec. 3, compensation is computed based on mutual evaluation of which factors?
o: Talents, skill, experience, effort and time required by the project
The size of the Architect's firm
n: Compensation isn't just a mechanical % — it reflects the Architect's talents, skill, experience, effort, and the time the project demands. [Source: Rule II, Sec. 3]

q: Per Sec. 3.1, the compensation method should let the Client do what?
n: One of the three core aims of the compensation method (per 3.1) is that the Client be able to know costs in advance, alongside being commensurate with services and reflecting value. [Source: Sec. 3.1]

q: Under Sec. 4.2.1, the Lump Sum or Fixed Fee method is generally used when:
o: The project scope is uncertain or evolving
The scope of services can be clearly and fully defined at the outset
Only for interim or short-term engagements
n: Lump Sum/Fixed Fee requires the scope to be fully known upfront so the Architect can prepare an accurate work-hour and overhead estimate before quoting a single figure. [Source: Sec. 4.2, 4.2.1]

q: Per Sec. 4.2.2, what two methods are generally used to arrive at a lump-sum figure?
o: A government-fixed table and a Client-set cap
A percentage of PPCC, and direct build-up of cost-outline elements plus profit
Hourly billing and per diem rates
n: The two approaches — a percentage-of-cost shortcut and a bottom-up cost-outline build-up — are often used together, each checking the other's reasonableness. [Source: Sec. 4.2.2]

q: Per Sec. 4.3.2, Time-Basis compensation is typically used for what kinds of engagements?
o: Services not well defined, pre-design, partial/additional services, expert-witness or specialist work
n: Time-basis fees suit engagements that are hard to scope in advance or are short/interim in nature — pre-design, partial, additional, expert-witness, and specialist-consultancy work. [Source: Sec. 4.3.2]

q: Per Sec. 4.3.8, the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method applies only to what category of work, and why?
o: All architectural and engineering design work
Non-creative work only (accounting, secretarial, research, report preparation)
n: Because creative design value can't be fairly measured by hours spent, this method is restricted to non-creative tasks like accounting, secretarial work, research, and report preparation. [Source: Sec. 4.3.8]

q: Per Sec. 4.3.13, a Retainer arrangement is used when:
o: Services are needed only once, on a single occasion
Services are expected at intervals over a period, for a minimum service obligation
n: A retainer suits clients who want an Architect on-call without full-time engagement — a fixed regular amount for a minimum service obligation, with extra work billed separately. [Source: Sec. 4.3.13]

q: For a Group 2 building (e.g., a school or office building) with PCC of P50.0M or less, the DAEDS RPF is:
n: Group 2 (moderate-complexity buildings like schools, offices, malls) sits between Group 1 (5%) and Group 3 (7%) at a 6% base DAEDS rate for PCC up to P50M. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 2]

q: For a Group 3 building (e.g., a hospital or airport) with PCC of P50.0M or less, the DAEDS RPF is:
n: Group 3 (hospitals, airports, hotels, and similarly complex facilities) requires the greatest research/engineering input among the three research-heavy groups, hence the highest base DAEDS rate of 7%. [Source: Sec. 6.3, Group 3]

q: Which fee adjustment factor specifically covers certification costs for programs like LEED®, GREEEN®, or BERDE®?
n: Sec. 6.5.4 specifically calls out certification costs for green-building programs like LEED, GREEEN, and BERDE as a fee-adjustment factor. [Source: Sec. 6.5.4]

q: In an Architectural Design Competition (ADC), what is the Professional Advisor's role during Jury deliberations?
o: Casts the deciding vote on close calls
Is present during Jury deliberations but has no vote
Chairs the Jury and votes on all entries
Is barred from attending Jury deliberations
n: The Professional Advisor organizes and supervises the competition and assists the Jury during deliberations, but has no vote — the Jurors alone decide. [Source: Sec. 13.2, 13.2.3]

q: Per Sec. 13.4, how is the ADC Jury composed?
o: All Jurors must be lay members representing the Owner
A majority of RLAs assisted by a lay Juror representing the Owner
Only the Professional Advisor and Technical Advisors
n: The Jury must be majority RLAs (licensed architects) to ensure technical competence, assisted by one lay Juror who represents the Owner's intentions. [Source: Sec. 13.4, 13.4.2]

q: SITUATIONAL: In a two-stage design competition, if no contract is signed within twelve (12) months of the Jury's award announcement, what happens?
o: The competition is voided and re-run
The winner is compensated a further sum equal to the first prize
The Owner is fined by the PRBoA
n: This protects the winner's interest if the Owner delays commissioning the project after a two-stage competition — a form of compensation for the extended wait. [Source: Sec. 13.6.5]

q: Under Sec. 14.1.1, a Filipino Professional Consulting Architect (FPCA) is defined as:
o: A Filipino citizen who is not necessarily a licensed architect
A Filipino citizen and RLA in good IAPOA standing
n: An FPCA must be both a Filipino citizen and a Registered/Licensed Architect in good standing with IAPOA, specializing in a recognized branch of the profession. [Source: Sec. 14.1.1]

q: If no qualified FPCA is available for a specialized consulting engagement, what does Sec. 14.1.1.3 require?
o: A minimum of two (2) Filipino RLAs must be employed as understudies
Only a Foreign Architect may be hired, with no conditions
The Owner must postpone the project by one year
n: This safeguard ensures Filipino professionals gain exposure/training on specialized engagements even when no qualified FPCA is on hand, before a Foreign Consultant may otherwise be relied upon. [Source: Sec. 14.1.1.3]

q: Per Sec. 15, it is unlawful for whom to collect a fee for architectural services?
o: A Construction Manager with a PCAB license
n: Only those registered/licensed under R.A. 9266 may lawfully collect fees for architectural services — practicing or billing without this standing is unlawful. [Source: Sec. 15]

q: Per Sec. 17, who bears government taxes (e.g., VAT) imposed on the Architect's services for a project?
o: The Architect, deducted from the Professional Fee
The Owner, since the Architect's fee is net to the Architect
Split equally between Architect and Owner
n: The Architect's fee is stated as net to the Architect, so any government tax on the services (like VAT), aside from income tax, is passed on to and shouldered by the Owner. [Source: Sec. 17]

q: SITUATIONAL (Annex E, Sorsogon Medical Center — DADS Worksheet): Starting from the 4.2% Group 3 DADS base and applying the equivalent adjustment factors, what is the adjusted sub-total fee rate?
n: DADS starts at a 4.2% base (60% of Group 3's 7.0% DAEDS rate); adding the same-nature adjustment factors (0.30+0.06+0.06+0.06+0.06+0.15 = 0.63%) brings the sub-total to 4.83%. [Source: Annex E — DADS Worksheet]
